Reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?
2. To be
referred to the Reporter or not?
Justice J.D.
Kapoor, President (Oral)
1. The aforesaid two appeals arise from
the order dated 30.10.2006 whereby the
appellant MGF Automobiles Ltd. was directed to
return the car to the respondent M/s. Neelam Trading Co. the consumer,
free from all defects and to make respondent consumer friendly and further that
whenever the complainant informed the OP about categorized defects in the car,
appellant will remove those defects free of charge, and further directed the
appellant as well as respondent-2 & 3 namely Himgiri Hyundai & Hyundai
Motor India Ltd. to pay Rs. 10,000/- as compensation for causing harassment and
mental agony and Rs. 2,000/- towards cost of litigation. The appellant as well as complainant M/s. MGF
Automobiles Ltd. feel aggrieved of the order itself as according to it the car
is not in its possession and is rather in the possession of respondent-2
Himgiri Hyundai and neither was this car sold to respondent-1 whereas appellant
M/s. Neelam Trading Co., the complainant is dissatisfied with the order
itself.
2. Since the parties arraigned and the
facts are little confusing, we for the sake of convenience refer M/s Hyundai
Motors Ltd., the manufacturer as OP-1, appellant MGF Automobiles Ltd. the
dealer as OP-2 and appellant M/s. Neelam Trading Co. as complainant and M/s.
Himgiri Hyundai, the service centre as OP-3, as arraigned in the complaint
before the District Forum.
3. The facts of the case leading to the
impugned order, in brief, are that the complainant purchased a Santro Xing car
from OP-1 and the said car was under the hire purchase agreement with ICICI
Bank Ltd. The instalments were being
paid regularly by the complainant without fail till date and insured with New
India Assurance Co. Ltd. That right
from the
beginning,
the said
car started
making noise
and the
complainant
complained
to O.P. No.1
who advised
the complainant to drive
the vehicle
for 15-20
days.
4. According
to OP-1, the vehicle would take some time to settle. The complainant had desired to purchase
EURO-III vehicle and paid Rs. 6,000/- extra for it and he was assured by OP-1
that it is a RURO-III vehicle. The
complainant stated that due
to the noise
coming 'from
the steering
wheel
as well
as from the
rear side
brakes,
he went to O.P.
No.1
for looking into
his complaint
but O.P.
No.1
initially insisted that there was no defect
and they
started
to say that the parts are not available
from the manufacturer and as soon as
the spare parts are received, the same would be changed. The steering assembly
was changed but
the noise didnt stop. The complainant complained
that he had been
given a vehicle with a definite manufacturing defect. The complainant
also approached
O.P. No.2 and O.P. No.3 but all went in vain.
The complainant
further stated that O. P.
No.1 and 2 opened each and every part of
the vehicle for their "Hit & Trial Method. O.P.
No.1 and 2 are trying their
best to pressurize
the complainant
to forgo an amount of Rs.75,000/-
and get the rest of the money back
but the complainant asked for a replacement and damages
or the entire refund with damages. The complainant stated that the
O.Ps started to threaten and pressurize him by
illegally asking him to pay for the "parking
charges"
but the
complainant
refused to take
the vehicle
which from
the very
inception
was not functioning
properly and
not a EURO-III
vehicle. The complainant prayed
before the District Forum
to direct
the O.P.
to pay Rs.5,20,000/-
to the complainant
towards
the cost of the vehicle,
conveyance
and stationery
charges,
compensation
for mental agony and loss
of work
and cost
of litigation.
5. As
against this the version of OP-1 was that the vehicle was delivered to the
complainant in a good and perfect running condition. OP-1 further submitted that the complainant was delivered with the EURO-III vehicle only and that whenever the
complainant visited, he was duly entertained and the vehicle was checked properly for any defect for which the complainant expressed satisfaction on the job by signing the invoice. O.P. No.1 further submitted that the delivered vehicle had no manufacturing defect at the time of delivery. OP-1 sent letters dated 26.9.2005 and 10.11.2005 informing the complainant to take delivery of the car and it has been constrained to levy parking charges as the complainant's car is unnecessarily occupying
workshop space. Denying any deficiency in services on its part, O.P. No.1 prayed for the dismissal of the complaint with costs.
6. The version of O.P. No.2 was that the car was purchased from O.P. No.1 and the complainant is not a consumer qua O.P. No.2 and does not come under the purview of
Consumer Protection
Act
. OP-2 submitted that there is no privity of contract between the complainant and O.P. No.2. O.P. No.2 denied that Mr. Gaurav Khanna is an employee of OP-2. and that the
complainants car reported at the workshop of O.P. No.2 on 20.7.2005 and the car was delivered to the complainant in good running condition. Denying any deficiency in services on its part, O.P. No.2 prayed for the dismissal of the complaint with costs.
7. O.P. No.3 stated that the complainant has not been supplied a used or a test driven vehicle and the said car is a EURO-III car. That the complainant
complained of noise, no noise was detected and the
car was delivered to the complainant in good running condition and the complainant expressed satisfaction on the job by signing the invoice. OP denied that the complainant again visited on 5.6.2005. The car was duly checked and no abnormality was found therein. Denying any deficiency in services on its part, O. P.
No.3 prayed for the dismissal of
the complaint.
8. In view of
the aforesaid versions of the OPs the District Forum observed that though the
complainant was delivered with the EURO-III vehicle but the vehicle was again
and again going for checkups and repairs and the OPs were taking the vehicle
themselves and burnt the petrol of the complainant in the guise of testing the
vehicle. If there was no problem with
the steering assembly, then why it was changed.? Moreover, for the past one
year, the vehicle was lying with the OPs and therefore the complainant was
deprived of the use of his car.
9. The above
referred observations of the District Forum have been challenged by the OP-2
M/s MGF Automobiles Limited appellant against whom the main order has been
passed firstly on the premise that the car was never sold by OP-2 and secondly
that the complainants car came only once on 20.7.05 at the workshop and the
car was delivered to the complainant in good running condition. Since the car is in possession of OP-3 as
such even if being a service centre, is not required to be visited with the
order as passed by the District Forum, as there was no deficiency in service on
its part. Thirdly, that the OP-2
repaired the car on 20.07.05 to the satisfaction of the complainant without
charging a single penny from him.
10. The learned
counsel has contended that the vehicle was duly repaired by it and not only
telephonically but through letters the complainant was requested to collect the
car but he did not collect the same and as such it has suffered the expenses
for parking the car for such a long time say for three years and no charges
were raised upon the complainant so far as the removal of defects were
concerned.
11. As against
this, the main grievance of the complainant is that the vehicle was highly
defective in spite of having been repaired by the OP-2 & 3. The defects were removed and therefore he
should have been either provided the cost of the vehicle or replaced with a new
car free from defects.
12. It is a
misconceived notion that unless and until the vehicle suffers from inherent
manufacturing defect it may not be declared as a defective vehicle. The onus lies heavily upon the manufacturer
to prove that the vehicle does not suffer from any inherent manufacturing
defect that may need its replacement or may need for refund of the cost of the
vehicle. Mere allegations as defective
of the vehicle are sufficient to shift this onus as to put another burden upon
the consumer who has already suffered at the hands of the manufacturer to incur
further expenses to engage an automobile expert to get the opinion whether it
has inherent manufacturing defect or not, is neither the requirement of the law
nor even otherwise prudent to make the consumer suffer further. It is
the duty of the District Forum to obtain expert opinion on its own, if there is
some doubt as to the extent of manufacturing defect.
13. Whenever a consumer decides to purchase a
brand new vehicle or goods at considerably high price and does not choose to
have a second or third hand vehicle the
minimum expectation of a consumer is
that he would not face inconvenience or physical discomfort or other kind of
financial loss etc. for getting the defects removed every second or third
day. Otherwise the very intention of a
consumer to go for a very costly brand new vehicle should suffer such a blow
that he would undergo immense mental agony, harassment, emotional suffering,
physical discomfort and would deem himself as subject of injustice.
14. If a vehicle is found to be suffering
from manufacturing defect the replacement may be ordered but if the vehicle
suffers from some or the other defects and has been taken time and again for
repair to the garage it reflects either the poor quality or a defective
vehicle.
15. Even
otherwise the onus to prove that the vehicle does not suffer from manufacturing
defect lies heavily on the manufacturer.
16. The concept
of warranty is altogether on different footing. Warranty only gives right to
the dealer or the manufacturer to charge from the consumer for the repairs done
by them are beyond the period of warranty. But by no way the warranty can
render the defective vehicle as qualitative and good vehicle. If a consumer
takes the vehicle time and again for removal of the defect continuously and
even after the expiry of the warranty period also these circumstances have to
be taken into consideration while declaring the vehicle as defective.
17. The
quality of vehicle has to be tested on the definition of word defective as
defined by
Section 2(1)(f)
of Consumer
Protection Act 1986, which means any
fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or
standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time
being in force or (under any contract, express or implied or} as is claimed by
the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any good.
18. In our view the endeavour of the Consumer Fora should be to
settle the dispute once for all and not
to relegate the parties to square one by entering into second bout of
litigation. Therefore the permanent solution is to ask for refund of the cost
of the goods and not to replace the vehicle by a new vehicle free from any
defect as the possibility of new goods being also defective or repairs being not
upto the satisfaction of the consumer cannot be ruled out and in such cases we
have order for the refund of the cost of the vehicle or adequate compensation
as to the mental agony, harassment, physical discomfort and emotional
sufferings. By making orders of the kind
that the District Forum has made or by making any other order except in the
form of refund of the price, the consumer dispute will never see the end,
though
Section 14 (1)
of the
Consumer Protection Act vests discretion in the District Forum that if the goods complained against suffer
from any of the defects specified in the complaint or that any of the
allegations contained in the complaint about the services are proved, it shall
issue an order to the opposite party directing him to [do] one or more of the
following things, namely:
(a) to remove the defect pointed out by the
appropriate laboratory from the goods in question;
(b) to replace the goods with new goods of similar
description which shall be free from any defect;
(c) to
return to the complainant the price, or, as the case may be, the charges paid
by the complainant;
(d) to pay such
amount as may be awarded by it as compensation to the consumer for any loss or
injury suffered by the consumer, due to the negligence of the opposite party;
(e) to remove
the effects or deficiencies in the services in question;
19. In the
given facts and circumstance of the case we dispose of all the appeals in the following
terms:-
(i) Hyundai
Motors Ltd., OP-3 shall refund the cost of the vehicle to the complainant with
depreciated value of 5% and shall collect the vehicle from its service centre
and the complainant shall fulfill all the necessary formalities for effecting
the change of the ownership in the registration certificate.
(ii) OP-3 the
manufacturer will pay compensation of Rs. 20,000/- to the complainant for
causing mental agony and harassment for selling a defective vehicle and Rs.
10,000/- as cost of litigation.
20. Order
against dealer and service centre M/s Himgiri Hyundai is set aside.
21. The payment shall be made within one
month from the date of receipt of this order.
22. Bank
Guarantee/FDR, if any furnished by the appellant, be returned forthwith.
23. A
copy of this order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the
parties free of charge and also to the 

 

  

 

  

 

  

 

concerned District Forum and thereafter the
file be consigned to Record room.
24. Announced
on 1st day of December, 2008.
(Justice J.D. Kapoor) 

 

President 

 

  

 

  

 

  

 

(Rumnita Mittal)
